title: Typed Hooks (TypeScript)
definition: Creating pre-typed versions of `useDispatch` and `useSelector` in TypeScript to avoid having to manually type `(state: RootState)` every time you select data.
simpleExplanation: In TypeScript, `useSelector((state) => state.auth)` will throw an error because TS doesn't know what `state` looks like. You create a custom `useAppSelector` hook once, tell it what your state looks like, and use that custom hook everywhere in your app instead.
realWorldExample: Creating an `hooks.ts` file in your Redux folder that exports `useAppDispatch` and `useAppSelector`, and mandating that developers use those instead of the default React-Redux hooks.

basic: Which two hooks do you usually recreate for TypeScript?
intermediate: Why do you need a typed version of `useDispatch`?

answers.question: Why type dispatch?
answers.answer: If you are using Redux Thunk (async actions), the default `Dispatch` type doesn't know how to handle Thunks. `AppDispatch` fixes this, enabling autocomplete for your async actions.
